## Why This Is Asked
Assess practical understanding of cache coherence in a high‑throughput, GPU‑accelerated setting.

## Key Concepts
- Directory‑based CCA
- MESI‑like states and transitions
- Atomic primitives (CAS, load, store)
- Granularity vs traffic trade-offs

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-layout for a vertex cache line
class VertexCacheLine {
  constructor(owner, sharersMask, version, payload){
    this.owner = owner; // int GPU id or -1
    this.sharers = sharersMask; // bitmap
    this.version = version; // int32
    this.payload = payload; // 64-bit data blob
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure coherence traffic versus computation throughput?
- How would you handle dynamic GPU membership (hot swap, failures)?

## Why This Is Asked

Real-time streaming of cca_score requires robust ingestion, isolation by tenant, and fault-tolerant aggregation to meet latency targets and privacy budgets. This question probes end-to-end design skills, from data modeling to stream processing choices and testing.

## Key Concepts

- Streaming ingestion and exactly-once vs at-least-once semantics
- Per-tenant privacy budgets and isolation
- Windowed aggregation and state management
- Backpressure handling, fault tolerance, and replay safety

## Code Example

```java
// Flink pseudo
DataStream<ScoreShare> input = ...

DataStream<Aggregated> agg = input
  .keyBy(s -> s.tenant_id)
  .window(TumblingEventTimeWindows.of(Time.minutes(1)))
  .reduce((a,b) -> new Aggregated(a.tenant_id, a.total + b.score_share, ...));
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you tune window size vs latency?
- What strategies would you use to detect poisoning in a streaming pipeline?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to design multi-tenant, hardware-attested, versioned scoring pipelines with safe migrations and robust auditing for privacy-preserving systems.

## Key Concepts
- Hardware attestation integration across multiple TPM providers
- Versioned policy enforcement and schema evolution
- End-to-end provenance tracking per attestation
- Replay protection and tamper-evidence mechanisms
- Cross-version compatibility and safe rollback procedures

## Testing Strategy

### Attestation Integrity Testing
- Replay attack prevention using nonce-based challenges
- Signature validation across different TPM manufacturers
- Attestation blob tamper detection with cryptographic hash verification
- Cross-TPM compatibility testing with known good attestation samples

### Cross-Version Compatibility Testing
- Automated schema migration testing between policy versions
- Backward compatibility verification for legacy client submissions
- Score consistency validation across policy version boundaries
- Integration testing with sandboxed TPM emulators

### Audit and Rollback Strategy
- Immutable audit log for all attestation submissions and policy changes
- Time-bound rollback windows with automatic health check validation
- Canary deployments with real-time monitoring of attestation success rates
- Emergency rollback triggers with attestation replay verification
